question: Assume today is 2026-10-27. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of cars manufactured in the United Kingdom in September 2026 (total car production for home and export markets, excluding commercial vehicles), as it will be first reported in the Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders' (SMMT) monthly UK car manufacturing release.

target.what: Total number of cars (passenger cars, excluding commercial vehicles) manufactured in the United Kingdom in September 2026, counting both home-market and export production, as first reported in SMMT's monthly UK car manufacturing release
target.publisher: Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders (SMMT)
target.caveats: Target period is completed relative to the 2026-10-27 cutoff, but the SMMT September 2026 release (typically published mid-to-late October) may or may not yet be public at cutoff; the estimate is for the first-reported figure, which is subject to later revision. Definition is SMMT 'car production' =

candidates.hypothesis: September 2026 production is anchored by the same month in prior years (September 2023, 2024, 2025) and by the most recent months published before cutoff (July/August 2026), adjusted for trend and any known disruptions; September is typically a strong month due to new-model-year ramp-up.
candidates.data_to_find: SMMT UK car manufacturing figures for September 2023, September 2024, September 2025 (total, home, export), plus July 2026 and August 2026 totals if published before 2026-10-27. Minimum: at least two September observations and one recent 2026 month.

candidates.hypothesis: UK car production correlates with SMMT new car registrations (home share) and with UK car export volumes; the home/export split from recent months plus registration trends can constrain the total. Production ≈ home production + export production, where home production tracks registrations of UK-built cars.
candidates.data_to_find: SMMT September 2026 new car registrations (published early October, before cutoff) and recent monthly export volumes; the historical ratio of UK production to registrations and to exports. Minimum: September 2026 registrations total and the recent home/export production split.

candidates.perspective: UK vehicle assembly plants (Nissan Sunderland, Toyota Burnaston, JLR, Mini Oxford, Vauxhall Ellesmere Port, Bentley, McLaren, etc.)
candidates.hypothesis: Total September output = sum over plants of (line capacity × utilisation × operating days in September). Plant-level capacity and any announced shutdowns/line changes (e.g., JLR cyber incident recovery, model changeovers) constrain the total.
candidates.data_to_find: Installed capacity and typical monthly output per major UK car plant; any September 2026 production halts, shift changes, or ramp-ups announced before cutoff. Minimum: capacity estimates for the top 3-4 plants and any known September 2026 disruption.

candidates.hypothesis: September 2026 output deviates from seasonal norm due to identifiable shocks: JLR cyber-attack aftermath (2025), EV mandate adjustments, tariff effects on exports, model changeovers, or supply-chain issues. Quantify exposure to adjust the historical baseline.
candidates.data_to_find: News of UK car plant stoppages, strike action, supply shortages, or demand shifts affecting September 2026; SMMT commentary in the August/September 2026 releases. Minimum: confirmation of whether major plants operated normally in September 2026.

candidates.hypothesis: SMMT or industry forecasts for 2026 full-year car production, combined with the year-to-date total through August 2026, imply a September figure via seasonal share. Full-year forecast × September seasonal share ≈ September output.
candidates.data_to_find: SMMT 2026 full-year UK car production forecast (from the October 2025 or later outlook), year-to-date production through August 2026, and the historical September share of annual output. Minimum: one full-year forecast and YTD through August 2026.
search_hints: UK car output year to date August 2026

candidates.hypothesis: UK car exports (a large share of production) can be cross-checked against HMRC export data or EU import data for September 2026, providing an independent constraint on the export component and hence total production.
candidates.data_to_find: HMRC UK car export values/volumes for September 2026 (if released by cutoff), or EU/ACEA import data; the historical ratio of SMMT export production to HMRC export volumes. Minimum: one independent export volume estimate for September 2026.

assessment.note: All from the same SMMT September 2025 release as reported by Motor Trader: total 51,090 = home 12,269 + export 38,821, with consistent YoY changes. One underlying measurement, not independent confirmations.
Duplicate copies of the same September 2025 SMMT release, but mislabeled with 2026 periods. Values are September 2025 actuals; usable only as September 2025 history, not as 2026 data.
All report the same SMMT August 2026 car production figure of 39,328 (+6.1%). Single underlying source, many URLs.
Same SMMT August 2026 total vehicle production 40,872 (+5.7%). Consistent with 39,328 cars + 1,544 CV.

methods.rationale: Builds September 2026 from observed Jan-Aug 2026 cumulative (472,851) times a seasonal September share of the nine-month total, converted to a September level via a2/(1-a2). Anchors on the most recent actual YTD level rather than a depressed prior-year month. Failure mode: the seasonal share is an assumption; if September 2026 is disrupted the share is too high.

a1.role: September 2026 YoY change in UK car production

methods.rationale: September 2025 baseline (51,090, depressed by the JLR cyber stoppage) adjusted by an assumed September 2026 YoY change. Captures recovery from an abnormally low base. Shared dependency with m2 on SMMT data; m3 uses an assumption for the change while m2 uses an observed YTD level, so they are not fully independent.

assumptions.name: September 2026 YoY change in UK car production
assumptions.rationale: September 2025 was depressed (51,090, -27.1%) by the JLR cyber stoppage; August 2026 was +6.1% YoY and YTD losses eased to -3.9% (cars). A modest positive YoY change is plausible; JLR restructuring and weak EU/China exports cap upside. Range spans near-flat to strong recovery.
assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 is compared with the same month a year earlier and no major new disruption occurs.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of a fresh plant shutdown or a much stronger/weaker September 2026 SMMT release.

assumptions.name: September share of nine-month cumulative car production
assumptions.rationale: September is a plate-change month with new-model-year ramp-up, typically a strong production month; as a share of the Jan-Sep cumulative it is around 9% (one-ninth, slightly above average because September is seasonally strong). Range reflects normal seasonal variation.
assumptions.applies_when: The Jan-Aug 2026 cumulative is a representative base and September 2026 follows a normal seasonal pattern.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 is unusually weak or strong relative to the year's run-rate.

methods.label: m3

a1.role: September 2026 YoY change in UK car production

methods.rationale: September 2025 baseline (51,090, depressed by the JLR cyber stoppage) adjusted by an assumed September 2026 YoY change. Captures recovery from an abnormally low base. Shared dependency with m2 on SMMT data; m3 uses an assumption for the change while m2 uses an observed YTD level, so they are not fully independent.

combination.weight_gate: off: inverse backtest-error weights need a bank-level gate (>= 30 scored questions with >= 2 backtested routes, hit rate >= 0.7; METHODS_ZH 4.1), which has not been run

m1.note: Monte Carlo width below the default, not used to narrow

interval.rule: one block, so the interval is that block's own width

excluded_by_input_audit.label: m2
excluded_by_input_audit.reason: unit check: the formula's result is 'car/(64 month)' (car/(8 month) * (month/(9 month)) / (1 - month/(9 month)) = car/(8 month) * (1/9) / (8/9) = car/(8 month) * (1/8) = car/(64 month)), which is not a 'car' quantity: code could not work out the result unit from your input units: it adds or compares a quantity in 1 dimensionless with one in 0.111111 dimensionless, which are on different scales; convert one of them first

kept.name: September 2026 YoY change in UK car production
kept.rationale: September 2025 was depressed (51,090, -27.1%) by the JLR cyber stoppage; August 2026 was +6.1% YoY and YTD losses eased to -3.9% (cars). A modest positive YoY change is plausible; JLR restructuring and weak EU/China exports cap upside. Range spans near-flat to strong recovery.
kept.applies_when: September 2026 is compared with the same month a year earlier and no major new disruption occurs.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence of a fresh plant shutdown or a much stronger/weaker September 2026 SMMT release.

kept.name: September share of nine-month cumulative car production
kept.rationale: September is a plate-change month with new-model-year ramp-up, typically a strong production month; as a share of the Jan-Sep cumulative it is around 9% (one-ninth, slightly above average because September is seasonally strong). Range reflects normal seasonal variation.
kept.applies_when: The Jan-Aug 2026 cumulative is a representative base and September 2026 follows a normal seasonal pattern.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 is unusually weak or strong relative to the year's run-rate.

final.template:
The best estimate for total UK car production (passenger cars, home plus export, excluding commercial vehicles) in September 2026 is [[estimate]] [[unit]] ([[interval_level]] interval [[p10]] to [[p90]] [[unit]]).

The estimate rests on one observed baseline: September 2025 total car production of [[p1_value]], a month depressed by the JLR cyber stoppage. That figure is adjusted by an assumed September 2026 year-on-year change of [[a1_value]] (range [[a1_low]] to [[a1_high]]), reflecting August 2026 growth and easing year-to-date losses, capped by JLR restructuring and weak EU/China exports. The single method ([[m1_estimate]], weight [[m1_weight]]) is the whole estimate; no backtest error was available ([[m1_backtest_error]]), so the interval is conditional on the assumption rather than empirically calibrated.

The main risk is that the assumed recovery is wrong: the base month was abnormal, so the true rebound could be much larger or smaller. Better evidence would be the actual September 2026 SMMT release or reliable monthly production data bridging the gap.

Unit of the estimate: [[unit_full]].

Key assumptions (proposed by the analyst model, not observed; code samples each one between the bounds shown):
- a1 September 2026 YoY change in UK car production: [[a1_value]], range [[a1_low]] to [[a1_high]]; used by m1. Overturned by: Evidence of a fresh plant shutdown or a much stronger/weaker September 2026 SMMT release.

Method details (computed by code):
- m1 formula_mc: p1 * (1 + a1); Monte Carlo P10 to P90 [[m1_mc_p10]] to [[m1_mc_p90]]; result unit (car/month) * 1 month converted to car; own 80% width [[m1_width]] (no error evidence, code's default width)

final.text:
The best estimate for total UK car production (passenger cars, home plus export, excluding commercial vehicles) in September 2026 is 51,144 car (80% model-based interval 37,124 to 70,460 car).

The estimate rests on one observed baseline: September 2025 total car production of 51,090 car, a month depressed by the JLR cyber stoppage. That figure is adjusted by an assumed September 2026 year-on-year change of 0.02% (range 0.001% to 0.12%), reflecting August 2026 growth and easing year-to-date losses, capped by JLR restructuring and weak EU/China exports. The single method (51,144, weight 100%) is the whole estimate; no backtest error was available (n/a), so the interval is conditional on the assumption rather than empirically calibrated.

The main risk is that the assumed recovery is wrong: the base month was abnormal, so the true rebound could be much larger or smaller. Better evidence would be the actual September 2026 SMMT release or reliable monthly production data bridging the gap.

Unit of the estimate: car (total for 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-30).

Key assumptions (proposed by the analyst model, not observed; code samples each one between the bounds shown):
- a1 September 2026 YoY change in UK car production: 0.02%, range 0.001% to 0.12%; used by m1. Overturned by: Evidence of a fresh plant shutdown or a much stronger/weaker September 2026 SMMT release.

Method details (computed by code):
- m1 formula_mc: p1 * (1 + a1); Monte Carlo P10 to P90 42,666 to 61,481; result unit (car/month) * 1 month converted to car; own 80% width x/÷1.38 (no error evidence, code's default width)
- Combination: 1 block(s), equal weight per block (methods whose inputs overlap by at least half form one block; backtest errors set widths, not weights): B1 = m1: 51,144 (width x/÷1.38, no error evidence, code's default width). Estimate = the only block.
- Interval: one block, so the interval is that block's own width (x/÷1.38).

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
